claim: With the support table removed from the prompt, a fixed closed-form low-rank update on the top two MLP layers of a frozen model answers questions about nouns that are not in a 20-example-per-group table (it must place the new noun in one of the table's four groups and return that group's code) within 5 points of the unmodified model given the table in its prompt, on tables built from the 37 confirmation item groups.

controls.most_frequent_code: mfc_bare must score exactly 25% on every table; anything else invalidates the run
controls.wrong_labels: shuf_bare and shuf_ctx reported against top2_bare and top2_ctx, table-level; if the wrong-label adapter is not below the real one (sign-flip p < 0.05), the write-up says the result is not shown to be information from the table
controls.plain_classifier: probe_bare against top2_bare on the same rows, read from the 90% paired-bootstrap interval on per-table (adapter minus classifier) (gate_v5.py, tie_rule). Owner's rule: stop, close the practical adapter claim and publish the readout result if the classifier matches or beats the adapter (mean difference at or below 0), or if the adapter's upside is capped below 5 points (interval upper bound under +5) and the cached prompt shows no clear residency win. Advance to the 96-table confirmation only if the adapter shows real upside over both the classifier and cached-prompt residency.
controls.tie_definition: Confirmed by the owner on 2026-11-19: a true tie requires the interval on (adapter minus classifier) to lie inside -5 to +5 points. A difference that is merely not significant is not a tie; an interval too wide to show either is reported as inconclusive and needs more tables.
controls.nearest_neighbour: nn_bare against top2_bare and against probe_bare on the same rows, reported with the same interval and reading as the plain classifier. The owner's stop rule is applied to the plain classifier; if the nearest-neighbour vote does better than the plain classifier, the write-up says so and applies the same reading to it.

scope_note: The task is classification by example: every question is about a noun that does not appear in the table. Nothing here tests recall of a stored item (arbitrary item-to-code lookup); that would be a separate experiment. The simple ways to do this task are the controls: a nearest-neighbour vote and a plain classifier over the same activations, and the cached prompt.

faast.reference: Bao et al., 'FAAST: Forward-Only Associative Learning via Closed-Form Fast Weights for Test-Time Supervised Adaptation', arXiv 2605.04651, submitted 6 May 2026; code at github.com/baoguangsheng/faast
faast.read: 2026-11-19, the arXiv abstract and the first 100,000 characters of the HTML through a summarising fetch; the appendix was not read. Read the method in full before confirmation.
faast.what_it_does: Compiles labelled examples into fast weights in closed form (least squares with a filtered pseudoinverse), with no gradient step at adaptation time, and discards the examples afterwards. For language models it adds a fast-weight matrix per layer whose output returns through a readout projection that is trained once and then frozen. Evaluated on image classification (frozen CLIP ResNet-50), sentiment and language modelling (GPT-2 family) and translation (Qwen2.5 3B and 7B Instruct), against linear projection, kNN memory, LoRA, in-context learning and kNN-LM. No cached-prompt baseline in the part read.
faast.consequence_for_this_study: Compiling labelled examples into weights in closed form without a gradient step is not new, and this study does not claim it. What is tested here is a systems result: with the table removed, accuracy within 5 points of the model given the table (or its cached prompt), with how much less state and time, on Q4K models in Doppler's WebGPU runtime, writing into an existing MLP weight with no trained component.
faast.differences: FAAST adds a module with a trained readout and reads hidden states; v5 writes a low-rank update into the existing down_proj of the top two layers, aimed at output-token directions, with nothing trained. In FAAST's few-shot classification tables its closed-form map, a linear probe and kNN are within about 2 points of each other, which is what this study's classifier and nearest-neighbour controls test for here.
faast.as_a_baseline: It has released code and models, so it is a direct baseline. Running it needs its code and a model it supports, which are downloads and a second runtime: an owner decision, listed in still_required_before_lock.
